articles.title: Finda a 'Equilibrium tour', Anitta anuncia agenda do show carnavalesco que fará no verão, em janeiro, por oito cidades | G1
articles.body:
Anitta fará oito apresentações dos 'Ensaios da Anitta' ao longo dos fins de semana de janeiro — Foto: Reprodução / X Anitta

♬ Mal Anitta cumpriu a agenda do show da “Equilibrium tour” , a artista já promove a turnê carnavalesca que fará por oito cidades do Brasil ao longo de janeiro de 2027, em pleno verão. O já tradicional “Ensaios da Anitta” terá em 2027 o tema “É festa no Brasil!”.

O cronograma da turnê carnavalesca prevê oito shows nos fins de semana de janeiro, em rota que começará por Belém (PA), em 9 de janeiro, e terminará em São Paulo (SP) em 31 de janeiro. No caminho, a artista fará “Ensaios da Anitta” em Recife (PE), Belo Horizonte (MG), Brasília (DF), Campinas (SP), Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e Curitiba (PR).

As vendas iniciarão na terça-feira, 1º de setembro, para clientes com o cartão do patrocinador da turnê. Na quarta-feira, 2 de setembro, as vendas abrirão para o público em geral.

articles.title: Zé Maria, ex-presidente do Colo-Colo, aos 72 anos na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-dirigente do time de Ilhéus faleceu neste domingo (30), na cidade. José Maria Almeida de Santana era reconhecido também por seu trabalho como comunicador.
articles.summary: Ex-dirigente do time de Ilhéus faleceu neste domingo (30), na cidade. José Maria Almeida de Santana era reconhecido também por seu trabalho como comunicador.
articles.body:
Morre Zé Maria, ex-presidente do Colo-Colo-, aos 72 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O desportista, jornalista e radialista José Maria Almeida de Santana morreu neste domingo (30), aos 72 anos, em Ilhéus , no sul da Bahia. Zé Maria , como era mais conhecido, é lembrado como "eterno presidente" do Colo-Colo de Futebol e Regatas , time da cidade que conquistou suas maiores glórias quando comandado pelo dirigente.

Conforme apurado pela TV Santa Cruz, afiliada da TV Bahia na região, ele sofreu um infarto agudo do miocárdio e não resistiu.

O desportista esteve à frente do Colo-Colo entre 1992 e 2011. No ano de 2006, o clube venceu o Campeonato Baiano da Série A.

Ao lamentar a morte do ex-dirigente nas redes sociais, o time relembrou a trajetória dele:

"Zé Maria assumiu o Tigre ainda em um período de futebol amador e foi responsável por conduzir o clube ao profissionalismo, disputando e conquistando o título da Série B do Campeonato Baiano em 1999. Sob seu comando, o Colo-Colo permaneceu por 12 anos consecutivos na primeira divisão estadual", elencou alguns feitos.

O ex-dirigente se destacou também como comentarista e comunicador. Em nota, a Associação Baiana de Imprensa (ABI) destacou que ele foi um dos fundadores da Regional Sul da entidade na região, além de colunista em diversos jornais regionais e criador do Troféu Imprensa do Sul da Bahia.

Como ressaltou a ABI, Zé Maria seguia na ativa como comentarista esportivo no programa Gabriela Esportiva, da rádio Gabriela FM, em Ilhéus.

"Nesse momento de tristeza e dor, externamos nossa solidariedade aos familiares, amigos e colegas da imprensa e da crônica esportiva", disse a ABI.

Colo-Colo manifestou pesar pela morte de seu 'eterno presidente' — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A Prefeitura de Ilhéus se manifestou com a publicação de um decreto de luto oficial no município. Válida por três dias, a medida leva em conta os anos de dedicação e amor destinados pelo comunicador ao esporte, seu pioneirismo e dinamismo cultural e o "feito histórico que colocou Ilhéus no ápice do futebol estadual", entre outros destaques da carreira.

O velório de Zé Maria ocorre nesta tarde, na SAF, no bairro Conquista, conforme divulgado pelo Colo-Colo no Instagram. O sepultamento será na manhã de segunda-feira (31), no Cemitério do Pontal.

Veja mais notícias do estado no g1 Bahia .

articles.title: Trabalhador que morreu ao cair de alegoria do Festival de Cirandas de Manacapuru é velado no Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Jone Salgado, de 45 anos, fazia parte da equipe responsável pela confecção das alegorias da Ciranda Flor Matizada. Velório ocorreu em Parintins.
articles.summary: Jone Salgado, de 45 anos, fazia parte da equipe responsável pela confecção das alegorias da Ciranda Flor Matizada. Velório ocorreu em Parintins.
articles.body:
O corpo do montador alegórico Jone Salgado foi velado neste domingo (30), por familiares e amigos, que prestaram as últimas homenagens e se despediram do artista.

Familiares, amigos e integrantes do meio cultural se reuniram na Funerária Bentes para a última despedida ao artista, marcada pela emoção e pelas homenagens à trajetória.

Jone Salgado tinha 45 anos, era montador alegórico e fazia parte da equipe responsável pela confecção das alegorias da Ciranda Flor Matizada, uma das agremiações que participam do Festival de Cirandas de Manacapuru , no interior do Amazonas.

O trabalhador fazia parte de uma equipe de profissionais que veio de Parintins para trabalhar na confecção e montagem das alegorias da ciranda para o festival deste ano, que iniciou na sexta.

Jone Salgado, de 45 anos, vítima de queda de alegoria durante montagem para Festival de Cirandas em Manacapuru. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O acidente aconteceu na sexta-feira (28), na Arena Parque do Ingá, onde estavam sendo realizadas as montagens das alegorias para o Festival de Cirandas de Manacapuru.

Segundo informações de trabalhadores que estavam no local, Jone trabalhava dentro de um módulo alegórico e fazia a soldagem da cabeça de um dos bonecos. Após terminar o serviço, ele começou a descer pela estrutura.

Durante a descida, ele precisou trocar o equipamento de segurança. Jhone teria retirado o cinto que utilizava e, antes de conseguir recolocar o equipamento, escorregou ao se aproximar da base da alegoria.

Ainda conforme os relatos, ele pisou em uma área revestida por pano, perdeu o equilíbrio e caiu no solo. A queda ocorreu de uma altura estimada em 12 metros.

Jone foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital Regional de Manacapuru — Lázaro Reis, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

A Ciranda Flor Matizada lamentou a morte e afirmou que o artista deixou sua marca na história da ciranda e no coração de cada torcedor.

Morte ocorreu exatos quatro anos de outro acidente fatal no local

O acidente desta sexta-feira aconteceu exatamente quatro anos após outra tragédia durante o Festival de Cirandas de Manacapuru.

Em 28 de agosto de 2022, durante o 22º Festival de Cirandas, uma alegoria da Ciranda Flor Matizada que estava suspensa se desprendeu de um guindaste e caiu. A autônoma Vivian Ramos da Silva morreu e outras 25 pessoas ficaram feridas.

Na época, diversas vítimas foram internadas em unidades de saúde do Amazonas, algumas em estado grave. Vivian e os feridos eram integrantes da ciranda e participavam da apresentação no momento da tragédia.

O caso foi investigado pela Polícia Civil e, em 2023, a Justiça determinou que um técnico que despencou do guindaste recebesse R$ 70 mil de indenização.

articles.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla Make Major Announcement as Harry and Meghan Return to U.K.
articles.summary: It's been a week of big news for the British royal family. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have officially touched back down in the U.K. after six years state...
articles.body:
It's been a week of big news for the British royal family. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have officially touched back down in the U.K. after six years stateside. And, simultaneously, King Charles and Queen Camilla have announced a major autumn tour across the Caribbean, which will culminate in their attendance at the annual Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

Buckingham Palace announced that the sovereigns would visit the Bahamas, of which King Charles is head of state, followed by Guyana at the invitation of the president and at the request of the U.K. government. This will mark 60 years of diplomacy between the two countries.

The couple will conclude their tour with a stop in Antigua and Barbuda, of which King Charles is also head of state, followed by their participation in the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

The monarch's major announcement came on the heels of the news that his younger son was relocating back to Britain . The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are reportedly looking at homes in the Cotswolds , with the village of Stow-on-the-Wold seeming to be of particular interest. It would put Prince Harry within two hours of Windsor, where his estranged brother, Prince William , resides with his family.

The decision follows what was reportedly a successful London summer trip, where Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet were reunited with their grandparents for the first time in years. The children are due to be enrolled in a local school for the fall.

articles.title: Dolly Parton laid to rest in private Nashville funeral, family confirms
articles.summary: Parton was laid to rest Friday in a private Nashville funeral, her great-niece confirmed. Tennessee also moved to rename Nashville's airport in her honor.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the beloved "Queen of Country," died Aug. 25 at 80 after "bravely facing a brief battle with cancer," her publicist said .

President Trump ordered U.S. flags flown at half-staff through Sept. 1, while Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee instructed state flags to be lowered, as tributes poured in for one of America's most admired cultural figures.

On Friday, Lee and the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority announced they intend to rename Nashville International Airport in Parton's honor. The airport authority will take up the proposal at its Sept. 17 meeting. Parton's team told Lee they were "touched by the idea and open to continuing the conversation," according to a statement from the governor's office.

Parton was laid to rest Friday in a private Nashville funeral, her great-niece Lainey Mae Parton confirmed. She was buried beside her husband, Carl Dean, at Woodlawn Memorial Park, as her family had said would happen.

Here's what we know about plans to remember her.

Parton was buried Friday, Aug. 28, in a small private service for immediate family, in keeping with her wishes. Her great-niece, Lainey Mae Parton, confirmed the news in a tribute posted to Instagram on Saturday. No public memorial has been announced.

Parton told Entertainment Weekly in 2014 that she expected Whitney Houston's cover of her song "I Will Always Love You" to be played.

She also said she wanted the hymn "If We Never Meet Again" to be sung. Parton had long wanted the country-gospel hymn, previously recorded by Elvis Presley, to be part of her funeral, saying that it was her father's favorite.

"It's an old country-gospel church song that talks about, 'If we never meet again this side of heaven, I will meet you on that beautiful shore,'" she said. "That was my daddy's favorite. We did sing it at his funeral, and I would like it to be sung at mine."

She was buried beside her husband of 59 years, Carl Dean, at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in Nashville. The cemetery is also the final resting place of Dean's parents and several country music legends and friends of Parton, including collaborator Porter Wagoner. The cemetery is also the final resting place of Dean's parents and several country music legends and friends of Parton, including collaborator Porter Wagoner.

In the Instagram post announcing her death, Parton's nephew and longtime head of security, Bryan Seaver, detailed her request for a comfortable final resting spot. "Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton, because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest," Seaver said.

She is, however, expected to wear her signature high heels, TMZ reported.

While the funeral is set to be private, Parton's official channels are inviting fans to tag @DollyParton on social media and share their memories, or leave a message on her website .

In lieu of flowers, the family has asked that donations be made to Dolly Parton's Imagination Library , the book-gifting program for children she founded in honor of her father.

Several other efforts are also underway to honor the Queen of Country's legacy, including some arranged by Parton herself.

In 2015, Parton left behind a musical time capsule: an unreleased song titled "My Place in History," sealed inside a chestnut "Dream Box" on display at Dollywood's DreamMore Resort.

The box is not scheduled to be opened until Jan. 19, 2046, on what would have been Parton's 100th birthday. She spoke about it publicly over the years, joking to The Kelly Clarkson Show that the wait "bothered" her and that she wished she could dig it up early.

Alongside her musical legacy, Parton's philanthropic projects that she built over many decades will outlive her. A spokesperson confirmed on the day of her death that her Imagination Library program, which has distributed more than 300 million books to children, will continue. "The work ahead has never felt more meaningful, and we will carry it forward as she lifts us all up," the project said.

Dollywood temporarily closed Tuesday to mourn its founder, but plans to continue operating. In an Instagram statement, park president Eugene Naughton said it will carry forward her values of kindness and "dreaming big," adding that her presence remains "alive and well" there.

The Grand Ole Opry, where Parton was a member for nearly 60 years, will dedicate its Saturday night show to her. The sold-out tribute runs at 7 p.m. CT and will be livestreamed on the Opry's Facebook and YouTube channels. Carly Pearce, who began her career at Dollywood, is among the artists set to perform. A portion of ticket sales will go to the Imagination Library.

In Parton's home state of Tennessee, one lawmaker said he would float designating Sept. 25 as "9 to 5 Day," a nod to the title of her hit song. Legislators had proposed erecting a statue of Parton in 2021, but she asked them to withdraw the measure, saying she didn't feel comfortable being "put on a pedestal" while she was still alive, though she left open the possibility later on.

The Nashville International Airport push, first started by fans in a change.org petition in January 2025, gained official backing Friday morning when Lee and airport CEO Doug Kreulen announced the proposal. The petition had passed 160,000 signatures by Friday night.

The name change would make Parton the first woman honored on one of America's 50 busiest airports, according to the Associated Press. However, it is not automatic. The airport authority's current policy requires that people it honors have been dead for at least two years, and its board will address both the policy and Lee's proposal at its Sept. 17 meeting. Nashville Mayor Freddie O'Connell called the idea "wonderful."

Parton's manager, Danny Nozell, said that the singer also greenlit a number of projects before her death, including a biopic, a docuseries, a scripted series, an avatar show, a documentary about her upcoming Broadway musical and an animated series inspired by her children's book Billy the Kid .

Parton's goddaughter, Miley Cyrus, said she might turn to songwriting to process the loss. While the details of their closest moments would remain private, "Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong," she said in a tribute on Instagram.

images.caption: Several other efforts are also underway to honor the Queen of Country's legacy, including some arranged by Parton herself. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)
Flowers and signs are left in front of a mural of Dolly Parton in Ringgold, where the country music star married Carl Dean, in Georgia. (REUTERS / REUTERS)

articles.title: Dolly Parton laid to rest as niece shares emotional tribute to ‘Granny’
articles.summary: Lainey Mae Parton shared an emotional tribute to her "Granny" Dolly Parton, recalling 4 AM calls and singing together on the "Smoky Mountain DNA" album.
articles.body: Dolly Parton has been laid to rest, days after the country music icon died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, on Tuesday. On Saturday, Parton’s niece, Lainey Mae Parton, shared a heartfelt tribute to the late country music icon on Instagram, reflecting on the private moments and unwavering support she received from her "Granny." "This is a really hard post for me to make," Lainey Mae wrote. "I wanted to wait until after my granny was laid to rest yesterday before I tried to put any of this into words." STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING "From the time I was little, my granny always had a way of making me feel like I was enough," she continued. "She never made my dreams feel too big or made me feel like I couldn’t do something. She believed in me before I even knew how to believe in myself." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Lainey Mae said she could not think of a single bad memory with Parton and praised the singer for making her family feel deeply loved. DOLLY PARTON’S SIX-DECADE LOVE STORY WITH CARL DEAN BEGAN AT A LAUNDROMAT "Because she couldn’t have kids of her own, she always made us feel like we were hers," she wrote. "She loved us that way, and I’ll forever be grateful for that." One memory that stood out, Lainey Mae said, was being asked to sing with Parton on her "Smoky Mountain DNA" album while she was a freshman in high school. DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME "I was SO nervous," she recalled. "But she had a way of making me feel like nothing bad could happen. She made me feel safe, confident, and like I belonged right there beside her." Lainey Mae also remembered Parton’s support when she decided to attend beauty school instead of college. DOLLY PARTON SLEPT AS LITTLE AS 3 HOURS, DID HER OWN HAIR AND MAKEUP ON SET, CO-STAR DANICA MCKELLAR SAYS "She financially supported me through school and helped me get my career started," she wrote. "She didn’t just tell me to chase my dreams, she helped me get there." The singer’s niece said she was grateful for the opportunities and memories they shared, including appearing in a movie with Parton. "I have things I can watch, hear, and hold onto when I miss her," she wrote. "It still doesn’t feel real that she’s gone. I’m going to miss her voice, her laugh, her hugs, and just knowing she was there. I’m even going to miss those 4 AM calls, and I’d give anything to see her name pop up on my phone again." "I feel incredibly lucky that I got to call her my granny," Lainey Mae concluded. "Thank you for always believing in me, loving me, and making me feel like I could do anything. I love you, Granny. Always." Parton died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, on Tuesday following a brief battle with cancer, according to a press release. She was surrounded by loved ones at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center. "Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched," her team said in a statement. DOLLY PARTON'S ‘ALL-AMERICAN HEART’: HOW COUNTRY ICON FORGED SPECIAL BOND WITH US MILITARY "Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement continued. "Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly’s unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Parton’s decades-long career produced enduring hits including "Jolene," "Coat of Many Colors," "Here You Come Again," "9 to 5," and "I Will Always Love You." The latter found global success when Whitney Houston recorded it for the 1992 film, "The Bodyguard." TENNESSEE MOVES TO RENAME NASHVILLE AIRPORT FOR DOLLY PARTON DAYS AFTER BELOVED ICON'S DEATH Parton made her feature film debut opposite Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in 1980’s "9 to 5." Parton later appeared in films including, "The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas," "Rhinestone," "Steel Magnolias," and "Joyful Noise." WATCH: Remembering Dolly Parton: Country music icon dies at 80 Parton was also known for her decades-long marriage to Carl Dean, who largely stayed out of the public eye during their nearly 60 years together. Dean died in March 2025. Beyond music, Parton built a business empire in her home state of Tennessee, with Dollywood becoming one of the state’s most popular attractions. Her charitable work through the Dollywood Foundation and Imagination Library also left a lasting impact. Parton wanted to be buried in a bed of soft cotton after spending a lifetime draped in rhinestones, according to a tribute from her nephew posted to Instagram on the day of her death. "Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because, after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest."

articles.title: Reading Festival: Messy singer Lola Young makes surprise final day appearance
articles.summary: The singer has been slowly returning to performing after taking a break last year to "work on myself".
articles.body:
Fans at the final day of Reading Festival were treated to a surprise set from singer Lola Young.

"I am backstage, the cat is out of the bag and I am going to be performing so see you... at the Grid stage," she teased on Instagram, before treating fans to hits including number one single Messy and One Thing.

Her performance marks the latest step in a return to the spotlight after she had to cancel a string of shows last year following an on-stage collapse in September.

Young also pulled out of the 2025 Reading festival due to a scheduling clash.

The weekend festival concludes on Sunday with a line-up including performances by drum and bass duo Chase & Status, and Florence + The Machine.

After Charli XCX ushered in her own new era with an electrifying set following her latest release Music, Fashion, Film, Young's return was welcomed by festival-goers in Reading on Sunday.

Young had cancelled her scheduled appearance at Reading Festival last year due to an "unavoidable scheduling conflict".

A month later, Young dropped her microphone, collapsed backwards and had to be helped off stage in front of a festival crowd in New York.

A few days later, she cancelled all shows "for the foreseeable future".

"I really hope you'll give me a second chance once I've had some time to work on myself and come back stronger," she posted in a message to fans at the time.

Young has sought treatment for drug dependency and told the Guardian in 2025 that addiction had dogged her for "a long time".

The pop star has since returned to performing with a small run of shows in the UK, starting with a London gig in March .

"It felt so right being back on stage," she wrote on social media shortly after, but said: "As tempting as it is to jump on a big tour I'm going to continue taking things slowly despite feeling so ready to perform more."

Before touching down in Reading, Young performed at the Electric Picnic Festival in the Republic of Ireland on Saturday.

Although she has returned to performing and released reflective single From Down Here in May this year, fans are still awaiting a fourth album.

Reading Festival winds down on Sunday night with a star-studded cast including indie icon Florence and the Machine, R&B hit-maker Loyle Carner, and Irish rap group Kneecap.

The festival's other site in Leeds, meanwhile, closes after performances from singer-songwriter Raye and multi award-winning rapper Dave on Sunday night.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival Was a Day Full of Superstars, Nonprofits, and Joy
articles.summary: On the ground at the inaugural event, which featured artists like Rodrigo, Chappell Roan, Doechii, Sara McLachlan and Stevie Nicks and an inspiring social me...
articles.body:
By the time Olivia Rodrigo hit the stage to headline the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival, the sun had set on a sweltering day, and anyone who was fading was sure to feel reenergized both from a welcome breeze and from Rodrigo's set. The superstar had promised special guests, and she delivered, bringing out Lilith Fair founder Sarah McLachlan, whose groundbreaking Nineties fest served as inspiration for Daisy Chain; Alanis Morissette, who stepped in for Karen O after she had a family emergency ; and Stevie Nicks. "I feel like I'm dreaming," Rodrigo told the crowd at Great Park in Irvine, California. "This is the best day of my fuckin' life!"

It certainly felt like the best dream ever for the crowd of mostly women and girls at the festival, which sold out in 30 minutes . The stacked lineup included trailblazers who inspired generations of women to pick up guitars, on-the-rise bands, and pop stars primed to meet the moment. Like Lilith Fair, the all-day celebration was more than just a music festival: It was an inclusive and much-needed gathering — uniting music fans while supporting important causes.

The day before the festival, Rodrigo talked about its philanthropic aims. "It's a real honor to announce that we are donating $10 million to be given directly to these 10 nonprofit partners that you just had the pleasure of hearing about," Rodrigo said at a press conference attended by 10 organizations that advocate for women and girls and were participating in the festival.

Those nonprofit participants included Baby2Baby , which provides children in need with basic necessities; Black Mamas Matter Alliance (BMMA), which advocates for Black mothers' rights and provides resources throughout and after pregnancy; Center for Reproductive Rights , a legal organization that advocates for reproductive rights and health care access for women worldwide; FreeFrom , which works to end gender-based violence by providing survivors with financial resources and more; Jhpiego , which provides critical health care to women and families worldwide; John Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health , which advances health equity for Indigenous communities worldwide; National Domestic Workers Alliance , which advocates for the rights of domestic workers; National Institute for Reproductive Health , which works to advance reproductive health care for all at the state and local level; National Women's Law Center , which fights for gender justice on the legal front and beyond; and Planned Parenthood , which works to protect, provide, and expand access to sexual and reproductive health care and education. Net proceeds from the event are being directed to Daisy Chain Fields Fund, which benefits those nonprofits.

When describing the way music, community, and action were joining together at Daisy Chain, one word came up regularly at the press conference: "joy." And that feeling was palpable throughout the grounds on Saturday.

Lines formed outside of Daisy Chain Reaction, the area where the nonprofits invited attendees to learn about their organizations while participating in crafts like assembling daisy chains and making flower crowns. Several fans, many dressed in Rodrigo-style baby doll dresses, said they were drawn to the event because of their love of the superstar, but also because they want a better world for women and girls. Alannie, 18, says that at her age, the ticket price was a big investment, but after learning Rodrigo's motive behind the fest, she wanted to participate. "I see it as a purpose, to give my money to all these foundations," she says.

A trio of early-thirties Filipina women — Nerissa, Christabel, and Monica — were also excited to support the nonprofits. "I very strongly resonate with the different organizations she was promoting," Nerissa says, adding that she's used Planned Parenthood's services in the past. Christabel adds, "I think it's such a beautiful thing that Olivia is creating a festival and a place for us all to gather to really empower, advance, and advocate for women and the organizations at Daisy Chain Reaction." Monica addressed the issue of representation, saying, "[Olivia] is Filipino, so she's representing our people, and also the lineup of amazing artists that she put together."

That lineup made for 14 sets and 10 hours of great music. Things kicked off with Quiet Light, the stage name of singer-medical student Riya Mahesh. She and her dancers slowly grooved, striking ballerina-style moves during "Postinternefame" from her 2026 mixtape Blue Angel Sparkling Silver 2 . Eli Miller, who performs under her first name, followed. Amid songs like "Nobody's Girl" and "Girl of Your Dreams," Eli delivered a powerful message about loving our neighbors, "no matter what they believe or don't." She also pledged money to some of the day's participating organizations.

"It's fucking hot right now," Rachel Chinouriri told the audience during her set. "The U.K. ain't like this." But Chinouriri kept the vibe going anyway, tearing through her tender 2025 single " Can We Talk About Isaac " while premiering material from her upcoming album I Think I Spoke Too Soon, "It's about my twenties, and realizing I'm not the person I thought I was," she said of the album. "And I can become whoever I want to be."

Following her performance, Chinouriri said she was excited to join the lineup, shouted out Lilith Fair, and gave kudos to Rodrigo for her inclusiveness when it came to the nonprofit partners. BMMA in particular is close to her heart. "It's really heartwarming to see [Rodrigo] take the initiative for that because sometimes Black women are very overlooked in many ways or not understood, especially in health care," she tells Rolling Stone . "I think that the level of thoughtfulness of that was so sweet."

Devon Again got the call to join the festival just last Thursday, after Katseye had to cancel due to member Megan Skiendiel's ankle injury. "I said, 'Duh bitch, obviously I wanna do it," she told the crowd. But Eyekons got a taste of Katseye's Lara Raj, Yoonchae Jeung, and Skiendiel, who appeared at the start of Devon's set to introduce nonprofit Baby2Baby. Afterward, Devon performed a country-tinged set, which included fan favorites "Skittles" and "Cherry Cola."

Die Spitz took the prize for calisthenics at Daisy Chain. The four-piece from Austin, Texas ripped through their midday set, where the blazing sun was no match for their energy (if a little hard on their face paint). At one point bassist Kate Halter did a full-on handstand. Die Spitz's all-girl metal was met warmly, so much so that singer ​​Eleanor Livingston jumped into the crowd to join the revelers.

Back in 2022, Santigold took a hiatus from the road, telling Rolling Stone about the "cultural crisis" and economic and mental-health challenges plaguing those who make music for a living. She resumed touring in 2024, though the dates have been selective and for short runs, which makes any chance to see her live special. Her Daisy Chain set was thoroughly joyful, including a dance contest and a bevy of fan-favorites like "L.E.S. Artistes," "Lights Out," and "Disparate Youth."

Feminist-punk trailblazers Bikini Kill, meanwhile, had taken a couple decades off, but came back hard for a reunion tour in 2019. They've barely slowed down since. "What a gift Olivia has given all of us to have this festival," singer Kathleen Hanna told the crowd. Like many of the bands here, Bikini Kill used their limited stage time to play the hits. Though they blazed through two songs from their last album, 1996's Reject All American , the band focused mostly on early songs, opening with "Double Dare Ya" from their 1992 EP, before sliding into "This Is Not a Test."

When Hanna told a story about a 40-year-old man creeping on her when she was 17 to introduce the track "Feels Blind," the crowd was rapt — "This is the most engaged crowd I've ever seen in my life," she said. Closing with "Suck My Left One" and "Rebel Girl," Hanna growled and danced her way across the stage, reminding the audience exactly why this band influenced a generation of women — and were integral to a festival like this ever coming into existence.

Mitski was feeling the communal spirit during her set in the late afternoon, telling the audience multiple times that she loved "every one of you." She had already put that love into practice with a series of PSAs concerning the extreme heat: advising fans to sit down right where you are if you're faint, head to the pit if you need water, and wear sunscreen. Of course, Mitski also delivered a stellar set, which included highlights from her 2026 album Nothing's About to Happen to Me like "Where's My Phone?" and "That White Cat," alongside fan-favorites like "Nobody." "I feel like we should do this every year," she said to loud cheers. "For the rest of our lives you can be like, 'Oh yeah, I'm OG DCF.'"

The Breeders have been in the Rodrigo camp for a few years now, opening up for the pop star on several dates of her GUTS tour. But their inclusion in the festival was part of the appeal of the lineup — the incredible mix of old and new. The fact that singer Kim Deal took the stage wearing a Shirley Chisholm shirt — referencing the first Black woman to serve in Congress — made their set feel all the more connected to the past. Starting their set with 1994's "Drivin' on 9," the band included other OG-era classics like "Do You Love Me Now?" and "Cannonball," while working in new, unreleased songs like "Alien Eyes," which they've been playing throughout their summer tour. Getting to test things out on the road, Deal told Paste magazine, is "like it was back in the old days."

When Doechii hit Lollapalooza in 2025 , she stole the show as headmaster of the school of hip-hop. At Daisy Chain, she signaled a new era, one that is pink-hued and incorporates all the right moves onstage. Wearing a bikini while covered in hot-pink body makeup, she and her equally pink-painted dancers delivered incredible choreography on a headlining-worthy stage setup, complete with a large riser, an LED screen and metal bars that Doechii at one point acrobatically flipped over. She had us from the jump, launching into "ExtraL," her 2025 collab with Jennie. Other collab tracks — the SZA team-up "Girl Get Up" and "Swamp Bitches," with Rico Nasty — hit hard, even if those artists weren't present Saturday. Doechii's mashups also landed: "Anxiety" sampled Gotye's "Somebody That I Used to Know," and Doechii freestyled over Beyoncé's "America Has a Problem," and even wove Britney Spears' "Toxic" into the mix. She ended one of the best performances of the day with a rousing version of "Denial Is a River," an instant-classic from 2024's Alligator Bites Never Heal .

Garbage's set was plagued by technical difficulties, but singer Shirley Manson kept her cool, joking that this was just the kind of thing the band was used to. "An entire career made up of this kind of carry on," she joked in her Scottish brogue. This, she said, was a lesson to the younger folks in the crowd: Even when things don't go the way you'd hoped, the world keeps spinning. "You don't have to be perfect," she said. "You can fuck up."

Despite the hurdles, the band delivered 1990s classics like "Only Happy When It Rains," "When I Grow Up," and "Stupid Girl" (which slipped into a brief cover of Bikini Kill's "Rebel Girl," much to the crowd's delight), as well as newer tracks like "There's No Future in Optimism" and "Chinese Fire Hose," off last year's Let All That We Imagine Be the Light .

Manson took breaks to address the audience, praising Rodrigo's ability to bring the multigenerational crowd together. "We've been around since before most of you were born," she said. "So to be included in this festival lineup is an immense privilege, and it's not one we take lightly." She also imparted some words of hope for these dark times. "I just want to assure you all — because I just turned 60, so I'm very old," she joked. "But if you just keep putting one foot in front of the other as you move through your life, I can guarantee you, it's like putting pennies in a bank. Sooner or later, you build the life that you want."

At the end of last year, Chappell Roan spoke about what she envisioned for 2026. She said it will be "the year of taking care of myself and others and really engaging in a community that feels real and not online. Volunteering locally and giving money to organizations I believe in." Daisy Chain was the perfect place for that, and the crowd erupted when Roan emerged onstage around 7 p.m., wearing a lavender set and matching boots.

Though the sweltering day had cooled down by then, "Hot to Go!" still felt incredibly fitting. Roan tore through other favorites off her 2023 smash debut The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess , including "Red Wine Supernova," "Pink Pony Club," and "Casual," plus the gem " Good Luck, Babe! " and her most recent single " The Subway ." When Roan appeared on the October, 2024 cover of Rolling Stone , Rodrigo spoke to us about the superstar. "I remember her walking into the studio one day and just flat-out saying 'I don't give a fuck about what people say anymore. If I like it, then it's good,'" Rodrigo said. "I could tell she actually meant it, too. That's her magic."

María Zardoya recorded the debut album for her solo project, Not for Radio , in a house in Upstate New York in the middle of winter, surrounded by snow and ice. The Daisy Chain locale could not have been more different. But Zardoya , best known as the singer of the Marias, brought a chill over the audience with a handful of tracks from Melt and her new EP, Bloom . Maybe it was the woodland-themed set over which she seemed to float, or the bittersweet subject matter — the project is partially inspired by a split from the Marias' drummer, Zardoya's longtime partner — or maybe it was just the fact that the sun finally went down, but Zardoya's set offered a moment of catharsis. With songs like "Puddle," "Swan," and "My Turn," she reminded the crowd that it's OK to be a little down sometimes, too.

Then it was time for Rodrigo, who capped off the night with a set that, appropriately, featured McLachlan. The pair performed McLachlan's 1997 hit "Building a Mystery," and dedicated "Angel" to Dolly Parton, who died on Aug. 25. They also treated the crowd to the live debut of Rodrigo's recent single " Serena Joy ."

Rodrigo next teamed up with Morissette — with whom she appeared on the cover of Rolling Stone in 2021 — for a scorching version of Morissette's classic "Ironic." Philanthropist Melinda French Gates joined Rodrigo and pledged to double the $10 million being donated. Rodrigo's final guest was Nicks. Together they performed a showstopping " Landslide ," which found the pair trading verses and dancing together. "She reminds me of me, when I was her age a hundred years ago," Nicks said of Rodrigo. "And I'm somewhat awestruck that she could do all this. Because it's so hard — you have no idea — putting this together with all of these people. And she's done it, with this grace." There were also plenty of Rodrigo's own classics, including "Bad Idea Right?," "Good 4 U," and " Drivers License ," the hit that first gave us a peek of the superstar she became, each drawing field-wide singalongs.

When Rodrigo announced Daisy Chain Fields, expectations were high, as fans hoped for a festival that delivered onstage and meet its mission for empowering women and girls. Saturday exceeded those expectations. And it turned out that Mitski may have been onto something when she suggested we do this again: "See you next year!" Rodrigo exclaimed at the end of her performance.

articles.title: Banbury Early Music Festival 'proud' of international award nomination
articles.summary: Oxfordshire festival says it is "a remarkable milestone" for an event established three years ago.
articles.body:
An Oxfordshire festival dedicated to medieval, renaissance and baroque music has been nominated for an international award.

The Banbury Early Music Festival said its nomination for Audience Project of the Year at the REMA Awards 2026 represented "a remarkable milestone for a festival established only three years ago".

This year's festival will take place on 26 and 27 September across the town centre before the team travels to Bruges, Belgium, for the awards ceremony on 25 November.

The festival directors said that while early music "can sometimes be perceived as something specialist or inaccessible" they had always "wanted to break down that barrier".

The REMA awards celebrate innovative and impactful projects shaping the early music sector in Europe and beyond.

European early music covers the period between 1250 and 1750, particularly when performed using musical instruments from the time, such as the lute, crumhorn and baroque violin.

The Banbury festival was established in 2023 by early musicians Dylan McCaig, Heidi Fardell and Alison Kinder, and has been bringing leading professional musicians together with amateur performers, young musicians, instrument makers, local organisations and audiences.

The nomination means it will represent the UK on the European stage alongside Team Recorder, a project created by recorder player, educator and YouTube personality Sarah Jeffery.

The directors said they were "enormously proud" seeing the festival on the international shortlist.

They said in a statement: "From the beginning, we wanted to create something firmly rooted in Banbury but ambitious enough to attract outstanding musicians and audiences from across the country.

"We strongly believe that people should not have to travel to a major city to experience world class music and culture."

They added that the mixture of renowned artists, local musicians, school pupils, amateurs and complete newcomers who took part in the festival made it "so exciting".

The nomination belongs "just as much to our audiences, volunteers, musicians, workshop participants, supporters and the wider Banbury community as it does to us", said the directors.

articles.title: Professor Murder Rides the Subway is a forgotten slice of dance punk perfection
articles.summary: Professor Murder Rides the Subway is the sound of mid-aughts Brooklyn in audio form.
articles.body: I recently dug out my CDs and started reripping them all. I’ve found a few forgotten gems in there, but few hit harder for me than the beautifully concise Professor Murder Rides the Subway EP. There was a period of time in the mid-aughts in NYC where it seemed like every indie band wanted you to let loose, dance like no one was watching, and just have some damn fun. Few embodied that as much as New York dance punk band Professor Murder. LCD Soundsystem and The Rapture were the biggest names of the dance punk revival. But there were also bands like Rahim, Liars, Dan Deacon, and countless lesser-known acts on DFA that you could see on any given weekend around NYC. And I spent a lot of time in those venues, shamelessly dancing my ass off to all of them. [Media: There’s something about Professor Murder’s specific blend of cheap synth blasts, shouted vocal chants, busy syncopated percussion, and throbbing bass that perfectly captures the vibe of the NYC music scene circa 2006. At their heart, the tracks on the 16-minute EP are built around a simple disco stomp (save for the brief a cappella of “Pedigree”). They’re dressed up with cowbell and other tuned percussion elements to add complexity. But they’re never allowed to disrupt the groove. While some of their contemporaries like LCD Soundsystem were chasing bigger, more melodic textures, Professor Murder trafficked in stripped-back arrangements where, arguably, the drums are the lead instrument. While there are hooks and melodies to grab on to, like the fuzzy bass on “Camron’s New Color (Part 3)”, they’re always a little quieter in the mix. The EP is bookended with two songs that are basically the Platonic ideal of 2000’s dance punk: “Champion” and “Free Stress Test.” If there was any justice in the world, the latter would have catapulted the band to at least Rapture levels of success. I dare you to not at least nod your head along to the beat. Professor Murder Rides the Subway is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including Apple Music, YouTube Music, Spotify, Deezer, and Qobuz.

articles.title: Camaru 2026: Portões abrem mais cedo com entrada gratuita no feriado  | G1
articles.standfirst: Além dos shows de Marco e Mário, que começa às 20h, e festival 'Uai Sô' o parque receberá também uma série de serviços ao longo do dia. Confira a programação que começa às 8h.
articles.summary: Camaru 2026 celebra o aniversário de Uberlândia com portões abertos, shows de Marco e Mário e Renato Teixeira, além de serviços públicos a partir das 8h.
articles.body:
Marco e Mário fazem o show oficial de retorno no Camaru 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Uberlândia completa 138 anos nesta segunda-feira, 31 de agosto. No aniversário da cidade, 62ª edição do Camaru - Exposição Agropecuária de Uberlândia, tem entrada gratuita para a população. O grande show da noite marco o retorno da dupla Marco e Mário aos palcos. O festival 'Uai Sô' , que começa às 12h, entre outras atrações, tem show de Renato Teixeira.

A Prefeitura de Uberlândia também leva vários serviços para o parque dentro do projeto Uberlândia Viva. Confira a programação e horários desta segunda-feira abaixo.

O Sindicato Rural de Uberlândia informou que será possível adquirir ingressos para o Espaço Varanda em todos os dias de programação gratuita. As vendas são feitas pelo site do Camaru ou na bilheteria do Parque de Exposições.

Nesta segunda-feira também será iniciada a programação da Cozinha Show, no Espaço do Produtor, e o tema do dia é a Produção Artesanal do Doce de Leite.

Formada em Uberlândia há mais de duas décadas, a dupla Marco e Mário retorna ao Camaru em um show marcado pela conexão com a cidade onde a carreira começou.

Para os irmãos, a apresentação durante as comemorações do aniversário do município representa a oportunidade de reviver momentos importantes ao lado do público que acompanhou a trajetória da dupla desde os primeiros passos.

Ao longo da carreira, Marco e Mário conquistaram projeção nacional com músicas que integraram trilhas sonoras de novelas e se tornaram sucessos do sertanejo. Entre os principais hits estão 'A Mulher Mais Feliz', 'Quem é Ela', 'Uma Chance' a 'Mais' e 'Flecha do Cupido'.

8h às 15h Cozinha Show - No Espaço do Produtor o tema é a produção artesanal do Doce de Leite

12h às 20h Festival 'Uai Sô' na Estância 34: 12h30 show de Luiz Salgado | 14h Show da banda Legião Rural | 15h Apresentação do Grupo de Catira Solas de Ouro | 20h show de Renato Teixeira | Feira de Artesanato das 12h às 22h

16h Liberação do acesso aos Camarotes/Lounges/Varanda

18h Liberação do acesso aos setores Prime/Golden

8h às 23h Parque de diversões (bilheteria própria de venda)

8h às 17h Fazendinha (entrada pelo bairro Santa Luzia - visitação gratuita)

9h às 14h Uberlândia Viva - Prefeitura Presente - Stands de várias secretarias oferecerão serviços e informações aos cidadãos. Estão confirmados Vacimóvel, Procon Móvel, informações sobre programa de estágios entre outros.

8h Provas Equestres - Ranch Sorting na Pista de Equinos

Cozinha Show destaca sabores e produtos típicos de Minas

Oficinas do Cozinha Show começam nesta segunda-feita (31) — Foto: Nara Souza/Divulgação

A programação da Cozinha Show no Camaru 2026 reúne oficinas, cursos e experiências gastronômicas gratuitas voltadas à valorização dos produtos e da culinária mineira. As atividades incluem capacitações em produção artesanal e harmonizações de queijos, cafés e vinhos, com realização do Sistema Faemg Senar e da Emater-MG. Informações sobre inscrições pelo (34) 98868-1786.

Nesta segunda-feira (31) acontece a prova equestre Ranch Sorting, uma modalidade de prova equestre que modalidade reúne duplas de cavaleiros que precisam separar o gado na sequência correta, com agilidade e precisão. A prova, que recebe competidores de várias regiões, acontece , a partir das 8h, na pista de equinos do parque.

Estacionamento: Para quem vai de carro, o Camaru oferece estacionamento pago que pode ser adquirido pelo site do evento ou na loja oficial no Terminal Central. O valor é R$ 60 para quem comprar antecipado. O acesso é pelo portão do lado direito da bilheteria.

Transporte Público: Para quem vai para o Camaru de ônibus, a Secretaria Municipal de Trânsito e Transportes (Settran) disponibilizará linhas especiais durante os dez dias do Camaru 2026. A linha S906 fará o trajeto Terminal Central/Camaru , com embarque na plataforma E do Terminal Central , enquanto as linhas S916, S917, S918, S926, S927, S928, S936, S937 e S938 atenderão o público após o encerramento do evento, com saída pela avenida João Mendes, no bairro Pampulha. Horários e itinerários podem ser consultados no Portal da Prefeitura ou pelo aplicativo UdiBus.

Transporte por aplicativo: Se possível, agende a corrida com antecedência e combine um ponto de encontro com o motorista que aceitar a corrida para a volta.

VÍDEOS: veja tudo sobre o Triângulo, Alto Paranaíba e Noroeste de Minas

articles.title: 'Toxic' box office collection day 5: Yash, Nayanthara, Kiara Advani starrer crosses Rs 200 crore India net; earns Rs 23 crore on Sunday
articles.summary: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' continued its theatrical run with another substantial collection on its fifth day. The Yash starrer has now moved .
articles.body: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' continued its theatrical run with another substantial collection on its fifth day. The Yash starrer has now moved past the Rs 200 crore mark in India net earnings.Toxic Movie ReviewAccording to Sacnilk, the movie collected Rs 23 crore net across India on Day 5. The figure came from 16,241 shows. Its cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 214.10 crore.The movie has earned Rs 255.95 crore in India gross so far. Its overseas gross currently stands at Rs 29.25 crore. This takes the worldwide gross collection of 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups' to Rs 285.20 crore.The latest numbers come after the movie recorded Rs 25.15 crore on Day 4 across 17,612 shows. The Sunday collection marks an 8.5% decline from the previous day's figure.Further, Day 5 recorded an overall occupancy of 25.2%.Hindi version remains biggest contributorThe Hindi version emerged as the top contributor to the Day 5 India net collection. It earned Rs 14.50 crore from 11,734 shows. The Kannada version followed with Rs 6.40 crore from 1,297 shows. It also recorded the strongest occupancy among the major language versions. The Telugu edition added Rs 1.40 crore from 1,541 shows. Tamil screenings contributed Rs 60 lakhs from 1,416 shows. The Malayalam version collected Rs 10 lakhs from 253 shows. The combined figures from all five versions resulted in the Rs 214.10 crore India net total.'Toxic' records varied occupancyThe Kannada version registered 55.44% overall occupancy on Day 5.
